issue.title: [Bug] [Build] DOCKERD for march cmd fails when there are conflicting directives in /etc/docker/daemon.json

failure.body:
#### Description

#### Steps to reproduce the issue:
1.  Check if there is a /etc/docker.daemon.json file and if not create one on the build server
2.  Add a directive for data-root
```
{
    "data-root": "/build/docker",
    ............
}
```
3. Run make config and try to build for a cross-architecture target.
4. Run this:
`NOJESSIE=1 NOSTRETCH=1 make docker-start`


Unfortunately, the actual error is not captured and is not written to stdout and thus the above output might not explicitly suggest what went wrong from the first glance

#### Describe the results you expected:

This shouldn't be seen

#### Triage:

Other useful internal commands to know about which are used internally in the Makefile.work:

**CMD which starts the slave docker:**
```
docker run --rm=true --privileged --init -v <build_dir>:/sonic -w /sonic -e http_proxy= -e https_proxy= -e no_proxy= -it -v /var/cache/sonic/artifacts:/dpkg_cache:rw -v /var/run/march/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v /var/run/march/docker.pid:/var/run/docker.pid -v /var/run/march/docker:/var/run/docker -v /var/lib/march/docker:/var/lib/docker`
```

As you can see, this expects a working `/var/run/march/docker.pid and /var/run/march/docker.sock` on the build server

**CMD which starts the docker daemon for building Cross-Arch Docker targets inside the slave docker:**
This command fails to start a new dockerd process and the error log is attached and should be self-explanatory
```
root@build-server:<build_dir>$ dockerd --experimental=true --storage-driver=vfs --data-root=/var/lib/march/docker --exec-root=/var/run/march/docker/ -H unix:///var/run/march/docker.sock -p /var/run/march/docker.pid
unable to configure the Docker daemon with file /etc/docker/daemon.json: the following directives are specified both as a flag and in the configuration file: data-root: (from flag: /var/lib/march/docker, from file: /builds2/docker)
```

#### Workaround:

add a `--config-file=` to the docker daemon start command, which then doesn't bother about what is in the daemon.json file

```
     SONIC_SERVICE_DOCKERD_FOR_MULTIARCH=y
-    SONIC_NATIVE_DOCKERD_FOR_MUTLIARCH := dockerd  --experimental=true --storage-driver=vfs \
+    SONIC_NATIVE_DOCKERD_FOR_MUTLIARCH := dockerd --config-file= --experimental=true --storage-driver=vfs \

     SONIC_NATIVE_DOCKERD_FOR_DOCKERFS := rm -fr $(PWD)/dockerfs; mkdir -p $(PWD)/dockerfs; sudo rm -fr /tmp/d; mkdir -p /tmp/d; ln -s -f $(PWD)/dockerfs $(D_ROOT); \
-                                       sudo dockerd --storage-driver=overlay2 --iptables=false \
+                                       sudo dockerd --config-file= --storage-driver=overlay2 --iptables=false \

```

#### Potential Solution:

IMO, the dockerd process should not be started by the Makefile.work itself. It should already be running on the build server and the Makefile can mount the running pid and sock files inside the slave docker

This is how the non-cross architecture builds operate. They doesn't kill/start a dockerd process but instead leverages the process which is already running on the build server

resolution.title: [build]: Add possibility to override dockerd config file for multiarch builds.
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it
Fixes #8898

Dockerd for multiarch build by default use host OS config file ("/etc/docker/daemon.json").
Default configuration used on host OS may not work for containers run inside sonic-slave.
"DOCKER_CONFIG_FILE_FOR_MULTIARCH" variable allows overriding path to the
config file that will be used for multiarch dockerd.

#### How I did it

Added "DOCKER_CONFIG_FILE_FOR_MULTIARCH" to Makefile.work file that allow to
override path to dockerd config file through environment variable:
```
DOCKER_CONFIG_FILE_FOR_MULTIARCH=${path_to_file}/daemon.json   make ...
```
If the env variable is not set build the system preserves its default behavior.

#### How to verify it
- Set DOCKER_CONFIG_FILE_FOR_MULTIARCH env variable
- Run build
- While build is running execute `ps -eo pid,cmd | grep "[0-9] dockerd.*march"` command
- Verify that `--config-file` parameter is set to the same path that was specified in DOCKER_CONFIG_FILE_FOR_MULTIARCH variable.
